summary: Starting from an all-cash $600 book, the three $65 buys take it to $195 invested (32.5%) across three different sectors, each at 10.83% of equity, under the 15% cap and inside each name's buy cap. There are no tax or wash-sale issues. Estimated loss in a 10% market drop goes from $0.00 to about -$8.04 (1.3% of equity), and IDXX accounts for roughly two-thirds of that.

checks.concentration: DPZ $65 / $600 equity = 10.83%, under the 15% cap and under its $76.20 buy cap. Consumer Staples sector weight after the trade is 10.83% (it is the only Staples name).
checks.overlap: No existing positions, so no overlap. Watch the label: DPZ is tagged Consumer Staples (SIC wholesale groceries), but it is economically a restaurant franchisor closer to Consumer Discretionary. A later buy of a real Discretionary or restaurant name would overlap more than the sector tags suggest.

In effect it adds financial-market exposure, which would overlap with any later MCO or similar buy that also carries an Industrials tag.
